### Marathon world record
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Marathon world record")]
In 2002, Radcliffe made the move up to the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)"), a decision that immediately paid off with victory at her debut in that year's [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") on 14 April 2002 in a world's best time for a women's only race (2:18:55).[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-74) Her time was the second quickest in women's marathon history behind the world record of 2:18:47 set by [Catherine Ndereba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Ndereba "Catherine Ndereba"), of [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), in Chicago.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-75)
Later that year, Radcliffe set a world record time of 2:17:18 in the [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon") on 13 October 2002,[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-76) breaking the previous record by a minute and a half.

### Marathon world record
She was appointed a [Member of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Member of the Order of the British Empire") (MBE) in the [2002 Birthday Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Birthday_Honours "2002 Birthday Honours") for services to athletics.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-77) She said: "It means a great deal to me, it's a great honour and it really tops off an amazing year. To come here and receive this and to meet the Queen at the end of it just finishes it off perfectly."[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-78)
Later the same year, she became the [BBC Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "BBC Sports Personality of the Year"), making her the first woman in over a decade to be honoured with the accolade. Paula thanked her husband Gary Lough, her coach Alex Stanton and her physio, Gerard Hartmann.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-79)

### Further world records
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Further world records")]
Radcliffe set her last women's marathon world record during the 2003 [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") in April, with a time of 2:15:25. The performance is one of the highest of score's values in terms of the IAAF World ranking points.
Radcliffe is the former world record holder for the women's road 10k in a time of 30 minutes and 21 seconds, which she set on 23 February 2003 in the [World's Best 10K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Best_10K "World's Best 10K") in [San Juan, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan,_Puerto_Rico "San Juan, Puerto Rico").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-80)
Radcliffe won the 2004 [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon") in a time of 2:23:10, beating [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya")'s [Susan Chepkemei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Chepkemei "Susan Chepkemei").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-81)

### 2004 Athens Olympics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2004 Athens Olympics")]
Radcliffe did not compete in the London Marathon in 2004, but was the favourite to win a gold medal in the marathon at the [Olympic Games in Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Olympic_Games "2004 Olympic Games"). However, she suffered an injury to her leg just two weeks prior to the event and had to use a high dose of anti-inflammatory drugs. This had an adverse effect on her [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach "Stomach"), hindering food absorption. She ended up withdrawing from the race after 36 km (22 mi). Five days later she started in the 10,000 metres but, still suffering from the effects of the marathon, retired with eight laps remaining.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-82) Radcliffe said "You go through bad stages in a marathon, but never as bad as that", "I've never before not been able to finish and I'm desperately trying to find a reason for what happened", "I just feel numb – this is something I worked so hard for."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-83)
Additionally, Radcliffe, like many other athletes, complained about the very high temperatures that prevailed in Athens at the time of the Olympic games.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-85)

### 2004 Athens Olympics
Regarded as Great Britain's best gold medal hope in athletics, her withdrawal made headlines in the UK, with editorial stances ranging from support to negativity, with some newspapers deriding Radcliffe for 'quitting', rather than going on to finish the race.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-86) Television pictures showed Radcliffe in a clearly distressed state after dropping out of the marathon, being comforted by two friends from her early running days.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-87)

### 2005: Marathon World Champion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: 2005: Marathon World Champion")]
[![Image 39](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Paula_Radcliffe_London_marathon_2005_crop.jpg/250px-Paula_Radcliffe_London_marathon_2005_crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_Radcliffe_London_marathon_2005_crop.jpg)
Paula Radcliffe leading the [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") in 2005, near to [Limehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limehouse "Limehouse") in east London.

### 2005: Marathon World Champion
At the 2005 London Marathon, Radcliffe won with a time of 2:17:42, a world's best time for a women's only race by over a minute. The race is remembered for a notorious moment towards the end when Radcliffe, hindered by [runner's diarrhoea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runner's_diarrhoea "Runner's diarrhoea") and in need for a toilet break, stopped and [defecated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defecated "Defecated") on the side of the road in view of the crowd and TV cameras which broadcast the incident live.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-88) After the race, she apologised to viewers and explained what happened, "I was losing time because I was having stomach cramps and I thought 'I just need to go and I'll be fine'. ... I didn't really want to resort to that in front of hundreds of thousands of people.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-89) Basically I needed to go. I started feeling it between 15 and 16 miles (26 km) and probably carried on too long before stopping. I must have eaten too much beforehand". In November 2006, the incident was voted _top running moment in history_ in the UK from a choice of ten "unforgettable moments".[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-90)

### 2005: Marathon World Champion
On 14 August 2005 at the [World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2005 World Championships in Athletics") held in [Helsinki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helsinki "Helsinki") she won Britain's only gold medal when she took the marathon title, dominating the race and setting a championship record time of 2:20:57. [Catherine Ndereba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Ndereba "Catherine Ndereba") of Kenya finished in second place, more than a minute behind. Radcliffe said: "It pretty much went according to plan. If somebody had been with me at the end I think I could have pushed it up a bit more." She and three other British runners were also awarded third place in the team competition.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-91)

### Family and autobiography
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Family and autobiography")]
[![Image 40](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Paula_%26_Isla_Radcliffe_2007_NYC.jpg/250px-Paula_%26_Isla_Radcliffe_2007_NYC.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_&_Isla_Radcliffe_2007_NYC.jpg)
Paula Radcliffe with daughter Isla at the New York City Marathon, 2007
Radcliffe took a break through the 2006 season owing to injuries and in July announced that she was expecting her first child. Her comeback was further delayed in 2007 as a result of a stress fracture in her lower back.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-92)
Radcliffe chose not to defend her world marathon crown in 2007, in order to undertake further rehabilitation, but insisted she wanted to compete in the next two Olympics. She made her return to competitive running on 30 September 2007, taking part in the BUPA [Great North Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_North_Run "Great North Run") in the UK on [Tyneside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyneside "Tyneside"). This was her first race in almost two years. Radcliffe finished second behind US runner [Kara Goucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kara_Goucher "Kara Goucher").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-93)
Radcliffe made her marathon return at the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon") on 4 November 2007 which she won with an official time of 2:23:09.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-94)

### Family and autobiography
Radcliffe released an autobiography in 2004, _Paula: My Story So Far_.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-95)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems")]
[![Image 41](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ae/Paula_Radcliffe.jpg/250px-Paula_Radcliffe.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_Radcliffe.jpg)
Paula Radcliffe at mile 14, New York City Marathon 2007
Radcliffe withdrew from the 2008 [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") due to a foot injury.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-96) Shortly after the London Marathon, it was also revealed that Radcliffe was suffering from an injury to her hip, preventing her from running. Originally thought to be a muscular problem, scans later revealed it was a [stress fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_fracture "Bone fracture") to her [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur "Femur"). Radcliffe won the 2008 Great South Run in 51 minutes 11 seconds, 11 seconds off of [Sonia O'Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonia_O'Sullivan "Sonia O'Sullivan")'s course record. In May, Radcliffe broke her left leg.
Radcliffe managed to get to fitness level for the 2008 Summer Olympics, but cramped during the marathon to the point where she had to stop running and stretch. She resumed the race and finished in 23rd place overall.

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe won the 2008 [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), making it her third victory at the competition with a time of 2:23:56. Russian [Lyudmila Petrova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyudmila_Petrova "Lyudmila Petrova") came in second, and American [Kara Goucher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kara_Goucher "Kara Goucher") took third.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-97)
Following the New York Marathon, Radcliffe suffered more injury setbacks: she had to withdraw from the [2009 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_London_Marathon "2009 London Marathon") due to a fractured toe. In March that year, she had a [bunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunion "Bunion") removed which doctors believed was the root cause of her other injuries at that time.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-98) She did not run competitively for almost 10 months, but made herself available for inclusion in the [2009 British team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain_at_the_2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "Great Britain at the 2009 World Championships in Athletics") for the [World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics"). She announced that the [New York City Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Half_Marathon "New York City Half Marathon") would be a testing ground for her fitness before the competition.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-99)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe went on to win the New York City Half Marathon in 1:09:45, two seconds off the course record. However, after this she pulled out of the World Championships as she felt unfit, and she missed the [2009 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "2009 IAAF World Half Marathon Championships") in [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham") due to a bout of [tonsillitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonsillitis "Tonsillitis").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-100) She returned to action at the 2009 New York City Marathon but failed to notch her third consecutive victory, instead fading to fourth place with knee problems.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-101)
[![Image 42](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Paula_Radcliffe_London_Marathon_2015.jpg/250px-Paula_Radcliffe_London_Marathon_2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paula_Radcliffe_London_Marathon_2015.jpg)
Radcliffe in the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon")

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Following a 19-month layoff that included the birth of her second child, Radcliffe returned to action at the Bupa London 10 km (6 mi), where she finished third, 55 seconds behind the winner, [Jo Pavey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Pavey "Jo Pavey"). Radcliffe called the performance "a bit of a disaster", and indicated she was suffering from a tear in one of the discs of her back.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-103)
Radcliffe set the [2011 Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Berlin_Marathon "2011 Berlin Marathon") as her comeback venue to try for an Olympic qualifying time. She came third in the race with a time of 2:23:46 — getting the Olympic standard and the fourth fastest time by a European that year.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-104) She was dissatisfied, however, saying: "I'm not particularly happy, either with my time or my place. I came here wanting to win".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-105) She used the 2012 [Vienna Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vienna_City_Marathon "Vienna City Marathon") to gauge her fitness and the race was set up as a battle between her and [Haile Gebrselassie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie "Haile Gebrselassie"), with Radcliffe receiving a head start of 7:52 (the difference between the two athletes' personal bests). She did not perform well and was comfortably beaten by the Ethiopian, while she crossed the line with a time of 72:03.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-106)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe pulled out of the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in London because of a foot injury.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-107) In January 2015, Radcliffe announced that she had decided to end her marathon career on 26 April 2015 by competing in the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-108) She finished in 2:36:55.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-109)
Radcliffe has served as a BBC pundit. During the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), she apologized for wishing volleyball player and convicted rapist [Steven van de Velde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_van_de_Velde "Steven van de Velde") good luck on the [Tonight with Andrew Marr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Marr "Andrew Marr") show.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-110)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
Radcliffe pulled out of the [2012 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") in London because of a foot injury.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-107) In January 2015, Radcliffe announced that she had decided to end her marathon career on 26 April 2015 by competing in the [2015 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_London_Marathon "2015 London Marathon").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-108) She finished in 2:36:55.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-109)
Radcliffe has served as a BBC pundit. During the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), she apologized for wishing volleyball player and convicted rapist [Steven van de Velde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_van_de_Velde "Steven van de Velde") good luck on the [Tonight with Andrew Marr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Marr "Andrew Marr") show.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-110)

### 2008–09: Beijing Olympics and fitness problems
In 2025, Radcliffe ran her first competitive marathon in a decade, finishing the [2025 Tokyo Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Tokyo_Marathon "2025 Tokyo Marathon") in 2:57:22.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-carney-111) She also registered to run in the [2025 Boston Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Boston_Marathon "2025 Boston Marathon"). She finished with a time of 2:53:44, winning her category.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-carney-111)
Radcliffe was appointed [Officer of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Officer_of_the_Order_of_the_British_Empire "Officer of the Order of the British Empire") (OBE) in the [2026 New Year Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_New_Year_Honours "2026 New Year Honours") for services to sport.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-112)

## Other achievements and awards
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Other achievements and awards")]
*   Awarded the [BBC London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_London "BBC London") Sports Awards 2003 for 'Sporting Moment of the Year'.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-113)  
*   Radcliffe has set numerous records, official and unofficial, on the track and the roads. As of November 2009, she holds the official world record for 10 km (6 mi) on roads.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-114) She has twice won the [World Half-Marathon championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"), twice the [World Cross-Country championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "IAAF World Cross Country Championships") (in 2001 and 2002), and in December 2003 became [European Cross-Country](https://web.archive.org/web/20071024100806/http://www.european-athletics.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=74&Itemid=119) champion for the second time, the only woman to have achieved this feat in the event's ten-year history.  

## Other achievements and awards
*   In 2004 Radcliffe joined with [Jonathan Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Edwards_(triple_jumper) "Jonathan Edwards (triple jumper)") on an _Olympic Special [Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Wants\_to\_Be\_a\_Millionaire%3F\_(British\_game\_show) "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? (British game show)")_. The pair raised £64,000 for charity, half of that sum going to the [British Olympic Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Olympic_Association "British Olympic Association") and a quarter of the sum going to [Asthma UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asthma_UK "Asthma UK").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-115)  
*   Nominated for the Sports Personality Award in 2007.  
*   Won the [Laureus World Comeback of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureus_World_Sports_Awards "Laureus World Sports Awards") award in early 2008 for her performances in 2007.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-116)  
*   Radcliffe won the Londoner of the Year award at the 2016 London Press Club awards despite being from Bedford.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-117)  
*   Radcliffe was made an Honorary Doctor of Technology ([Hon DTech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Technology "Doctor of Technology")) by her alma mater, [Loughborough University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loughborough_University "Loughborough University") in 2002.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-118)

## Other achievements and awards
Radcliffe now works as a pundit and commentator of athletics events for the BBC. She appeared as a pundit for the [Glasgow 2014 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow_2014 "Glasgow 2014") and [Rio 2016 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rio_2016 "Rio 2016").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-119)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-120) Following the retirement of [Brendan Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Foster "Brendan Foster"), Radcliffe has combined punditry with commentating on the long-distance events at the [Tokyo 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics") and [Paris 2024 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_2024_Olympics "Paris 2024 Olympics") and at the [Gold Coast 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Coast_2018 "Gold Coast 2018") and [Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham_2022 "Birmingham 2022").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-121)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-123)[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-124)

## Anti-doping activity
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Paula_Radcliffe&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Anti-doping activity")]
Radcliffe has frequently made high-profile condemnations of the [use of performance-enhancing drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Use_of_performance-enhancing_drugs_in_sport "Use of performance-enhancing drugs in sport") in athletics. Radcliffe and teammate [Hayley Tullett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayley_Tullett "Hayley Tullett") caused controversy when, in the heats of the 5,000 metres at the 2001 World Athletics Championships in [Edmonton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmonton "Edmonton"), they held up a sign protesting against the reinstatement of Russian athlete [Olga Yegorova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olga_Yegorova "Olga Yegorova") after Yegorova had tested positive for the banned substance [EPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erythropoietin "Erythropoietin"). The sign was made by Radcliffe's husband and read 'EPO Cheats Out'.

## Anti-doping activity
It was eventually taken off them by the stadium officials, but not before it was streamed around the world.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-2001_ED-125) After Radcliffe and Tullett's initial protest, teammates [Kathy Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Butler "Kathy Butler") and [Hayley Yelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hayley_Yelling "Hayley Yelling") – who both missed out on a place in the final – protested alongside coaches [Mark Rowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Rowland "Mark Rowland") and [Alan Storey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Storey?action=edit&redlink=1 "Alan Storey (page does not exist)"), wearing Radcliffe masks and holding up banners with mocking slogans including one which read 'Free Paula'.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-126) Radcliffe vowed to continue her fight against drugs in sport after her high-profile actions in Edmonton.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-127) Since the 1999 European Cup, Radcliffe wears a red ribbon when competing to show her support for blood testing as a method of catching drug cheats.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-2001_ED-125)[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-128)
> "We should be pleased. One of the biggest frauds has been caught. Her medals should also be taken away"
—Radcliffe on Marion Jones in 2007.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Jones-129)

## Anti-doping activity
Radcliffe has advocated a system where first time offenders are banned for four years and any future offence for life. However, she felt that in cases like that of [Christine Ohuruogu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Ohuruogu "Christine Ohuruogu"), who missed three out-of-competition drugs tests, that she should be allowed to compete in the Olympics, as the BOA does not allow anyone who has served a doping ban to compete.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-130) However, when Ohuruogu admitted to not trying to get to the tests, Radcliffe expressed her disappointment and hoped that it was a lesson learned.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-131) When [Marion Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion_Jones "Marion Jones") admitted to steroid use, Radcliffe stated that it was good for the sport that Jones was caught and that they had to keep testing and that people being caught is a big deterrent to would-be cheats.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Jones-129)
In 2019, regarding guidelines for gender in sport, Radcliffe stated “right now, transgender women are not a threat to female sport, but you would be naive if you thought that, by not putting in any rules, it couldn't come to that at some point in the future. People will manipulate this if there is an opening there to make money and win medals and we've seen the lengths people go to, the lengths Russia went to cheat in sport.”[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-132)

## Anti-doping activity
Reflecting upon the scepticism created by incidents of doping, she said "You have to accept the situation...it would be great if we could win the battle against doping and have testing that was 100 per-cent reliable, but I don't think that will happen in my competitive career." She has previously asked for the results of a [blood test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_test "Blood test") taken at the London Marathon to be made public, saying that she had "absolutely no objection to my test being released".[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-133)

## Anti-doping activity
In 2015, in the wake of revelations of widespread doping in athletics,[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-ST_report_suppressed-134) Radcliffe said that, unlike some other prominent British athletes, she would not be releasing her blood-test history, and discouraged other athletes from doing so.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-135) She was later indirectly identified as a suspected doper by MP [Jesse Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Norman "Jesse Norman") during a parliamentary inquiry into blood doping.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Graun_parliament-136)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Radcliffe_fighting_back-137) In response, Radcliffe issued a statement in which she "categorically denied" cheating in any form and said she has "nothing to hide".[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Radcliffe_response-138) Shortly afterwards, her three suspect test results were leaked, though Radcliffe still refused to release her complete blood-test history.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-Indie_bloods_leak-139) In late November 2015, the IAAF declared that the accusations were "based on the gross misinterpretation of incomplete data". The [UK Anti Doping Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Anti-Doping "UK Anti-Doping"), having received Radcliffe's blood test history via the IAAF, stated that "UKAD has come to the same conclusion as the IAAF review that there is no case to answer".[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-140)

## Anti-doping activity
Radcliffe was born to Peter and Pat Radcliffe[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-141) and is the grandniece of [1920 Olympic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swimming_at_the_1920_Summer_Olympics "Swimming at the 1920 Summer Olympics") silver medallist [Charlotte Radcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Radcliffe "Charlotte Radcliffe").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-sr-1)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-142) Radcliffe met her husband [Gary Lough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Lough "Gary Lough"), a former Northern Irish 1,500 m runner, when he was her lodger at [Loughborough University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loughborough_University "Loughborough University").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-143) The pair married in 2001.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-144) They have a daughter (born 2007)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-145) and a son (born 2010).[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Radcliffe#cite_note-146) The family resides in [Monte Carlo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Carlo "Monte Carlo").

**Tegla Chepkite Loroupe** (born 9 May 1973) is a former Kenyan [long-distance track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_track_event "Long-distance track event") and [road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") runner. She is also a global spokeswoman for peace, [women's rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_rights "Women's rights") and education. Loroupe holds the [world records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_record "World record") for 25 and 30 kilometers and previously held the world [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") record. She was the first African woman to hold the marathon World Record, which she held from 19 April 1998 until 30 September 2001. She is the three-time [World Half-Marathon champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAAF_World_Half_Marathon_Championships "IAAF World Half Marathon Championships"). Loroupe was also the first woman from Africa to win the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), which she has won twice. She has won marathons in London, [Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam "Rotterdam"), Hong Kong, [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") and Rome.
In 2016, she was the person organizing the Refugee Team for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics") in Rio.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)

Tegla Loroupe was born in Kapsait village in the Lelan division of [West Pokot District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Pokot_District "West Pokot District"). It is situated in the [Great Rift Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Rift_Valley,_Kenya "Great Rift Valley, Kenya"), approximately 600 kilometres north of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). Her father and mother are from the [Pokot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pokot_people "Pokot people") tribe, a [Nilotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nilotic_peoples "Nilotic peoples") ethnic group inhabiting parts of northern [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"), eastern [Uganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uganda "Uganda") and southern [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopia "Ethiopia").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3)
Loroupe was told by her father that she was useless and her career might be babysitting.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) She grew up with 24 siblings. The Pokots being a [polygamous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygamy "Polygamy") culture, her father had four wives. She spent her childhood working fields, tending cattle and looking after younger brothers and sisters.
At the age of six, Loroupe started school at Kapsait Elementary school; she had to run ten kilometers to and from school every morning. At school, she became aware of her potential as an [athlete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sportsperson "Sportsperson") when she won races held over a distance of 800 or 1500 meters against much older students. She decided to pursue a career as a runner. However, she was not supported by anyone but her mother.

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG/250px-Loroupe%2C_Tegla.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Loroupe,_Tegla.JPG)
Loroupe in 2007 at a meet in [Schortens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schortens "Schortens"), Germany.
The Kenyan athletics federation, [Athletics Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_Kenya "Athletics Kenya"), did not support her at first, thinking Loroupe too small and too thin. However, after she won a prestigious [cross country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-country_running "Cross-country running") barefoot race in 1988, this changed. She began to train to compete internationally the following year, earning her first pair of running shoes in 1989, which she wore only for particularly [rough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hazard "Hazard") races. She was nominated for the junior race of the [1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1989 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") finishing 28th. She competed again at the [1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1990 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"), finishing 16th in the junior race.

In 1994 and 1998, Loroupe won the [Goodwill Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodwill_Games "Goodwill Games") over 10,000 metres, [barefoot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barefoot_running "Barefoot running"). Over the same distance she won [bronze medals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronze_medal "Bronze medal") at the [World Athletics Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Athletics_Championships "World Athletics Championships") in [1995](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1995_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1995 World Championships in Athletics") and [1999](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Championships in Athletics").
In 1994, Loroupe ran her first major [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_(sport) "Marathon (sport)") in New York. Running against the world's strongest competition, she won. As a consequence she was [idolised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolatry "Idolatry") by many young people in Africa: at last, a woman champion to complement the many successful male runners. She won the New York City Marathon again in 1995 and finished 3rd in 1998.
Between 1997 and 1999, she won three world titles a row over the half marathon distance. She won [Rotterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotterdam_Marathon "Rotterdam Marathon") three times between 1997 and 1999. She won [Berlin Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin_Marathon "Berlin Marathon") in 1999 and finished second in 2001. She finished second at the 1999 [Osaka International Ladies Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka_International_Ladies_Marathon "Osaka International Ladies Marathon").

Loroupe won the [Zevenheuvelenloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zevenheuvelenloop "Zevenheuvelenloop") 15K race in the Netherland three times (1992, 1993 and 1998). She is a seven-time [Egmond Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egmond_Half_Marathon "Egmond Half Marathon") winner (1993–1998, 2000). She has won the [Lisbon Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisbon_Half_Marathon "Lisbon Half Marathon") a record six times: 1994–1997, 1999 and 2000.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-4) She has won the [Tilburg road race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tilburg_Ten_Miles "Tilburg Ten Miles"), a five times (1993, 1994, 1996, 1998, 1999), also a record number. She won the [Paris Half Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Half_Marathon "Paris Half Marathon") in 1994 and 1998,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-5)[City-Pier-City Loop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-Pier-City_Loop "City-Pier-City Loop") half marathon in [the Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague") in 1998,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-6) and the [Parelloop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parelloop "Parelloop") 10K in race in the [Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") in 1999.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-7)

During the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") in Sydney, favoured to win both the marathon and the 10,000 meters, she suffered from violent food poisoning the night before the race. Nevertheless, she fought through the marathon race, finishing 13th, then, the next day, ran the 10,000 metres, finishing 5th,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-sr-1) running barefoot in both races, a feat she later stated she achieved out of a sense of duty to all the people taking her as a bearer of hope in her home country. Until the end of 2001, she continued to suffer from various health problems.
In 2000, she won [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon") and [Rome City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome_City_Marathon "Rome City Marathon"). She also won [Lausanne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lausanne_Marathon "Lausanne Marathon") in 2002, [Cologne Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne_Marathon "Cologne Marathon") in 2003 and [Leipzig Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leipzig_Marathon "Leipzig Marathon") in 2004.
Loroupe competed at the [2005 World Championships marathon race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_World_Championships_in_Athletics_-_Women's_Marathon "2005 World Championships in Athletics - Women's Marathon") in Helsinki, [Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland"), but finished only 40th. In February 2006 she won the Hong Kong Half-Marathon. The same year she finished 5th in the Rotterdam Marathon and 2nd in the [Venice Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venice_Marathon "Venice Marathon"). In 2007, she participated again the New York City Marathon, finishing 8th.

Loroupe's biggest successes include world records over 20, 25 and 30 kilometers as well as the past record over the marathon distance. She used to hold the [One Hour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour_run "Hour run") running [World record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_records_in_athletics "World records in athletics") of 18,340 m set in [Borgholzhausen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgholzhausen "Borgholzhausen"), Germany, but the record was broken by Dire Tune of Ethiopia ten years later, in 2008 (new record 18,517 m).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-8)
In 2006, she was named a United Nations Ambassador of Sport by Secretary General [Kofi Annan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kofi_Annan "Kofi Annan"), together with [Roger Federer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Federer "Roger Federer"), tennis champion from Switzerland, [Elias Figueroa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elias_Figueroa "Elias Figueroa"), Latin American soccer legend from Chile, and [Katrina Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Webb "Katrina Webb") paralympics gold medalist from Australia. She is an International Sports Ambassador for the IAAF, the [International Association of Athletics Federations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Association_of_Athletics_Federations "International Association of Athletics Federations"), and for [UNICEF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF "UNICEF").
In 2003, Loroupe created an annual series of Peace Marathons sponsored by the Tegla Loroupe Peace Foundation "Peace Through Sports". Presidents, Prime Ministers, Ambassadors and government officials run with warriors and nomadic groups in her native Kenya, in Uganda and in Sudan, to bring peace to an area plagued by raiding warriors from battling tribes. In 2010 the Kenyan Government lauded her achievements as hundreds of warriors had laid down their weapons.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-9)

She has established a school ([Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe_Peace_Academy "Tegla Loroupe Peace Academy")) and orphanage for children from the region in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), a high-mountain town in north-west [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").
The 2006 Peace Marathon was held on 18 November 2006, in [Kapenguria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapenguria "Kapenguria"), Kenya. Two thousand warriors from six tribes competed. The next Peace Marathon was 15 November 2008 in Kapenguria, Kenya. National ambassadors to Kenya participated, together with the Prime Minister, and several Kenyan, Tanzanian, and Ugandan Ministers. The Peace Marathon has been held each year since then, with the exception of the past two Covid years. Winners of the races often begin professional training in long-distance running, or join the training team of ex-warriors.
In February 2007, she was named the [Oxfam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxfam "Oxfam") Ambassador of Sport and Peace to Darfur. In December 2006, she travelled with [George Clooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clooney "George Clooney"), [Joey Cheek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Cheek "Joey Cheek"), and [Don Cheadle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle "Don Cheadle") to Beijing, Cairo, and New York on a diplomatic mission to bring an end to violence in Darfur. She won the "Community Hero" category at the 2007 [Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Sports_Personality_of_the_Year "Kenyan Sports Personality of the Year") awards.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-10)

In November 2009, Tegla represented the [Shoe4Africa team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoe4Africa_team?action=edit&redlink=1 "Shoe4Africa team (page does not exist)").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-11) running the New York Marathon alongside founder Toby Tanser and actress [Sarah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Jones_(stage_actress) "Sarah Jones (stage actress)")[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-12) finishing in 3:54:02.
Loroupe is a member of the 'Champions for Peace' club, a group of 54 famous elite athletes committed to serving peace in the world through sport, created by [Peace and Sport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_and_Sport "Peace and Sport"), a [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco")-based international organisation.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-13)
As reported by Olympic news outlet [Around the Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Around_the_Rings "Around the Rings"), the IOC recognised six women, five from each continent and one to represent the world, for their achievements and their work to promote women's sport. Loroupe was awarded the world trophy.
In 2015 Loroupe became an Ambassador for the [Homeless World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeless_World_Cup "Homeless World Cup").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-14)

In 2016, she was the Chef de Mission organizing the [Refugee Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refugee_Olympic_Team_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Refugee Olympic Team at the 2016 Summer Olympics") for the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-nyt-3) At those games Loroupe was inducted into the [Olympians for life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Olympians_Association#Olympians_for_Life "World Olympians Association") project for her work in promoting peace.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-15) In October 2016 Loroupe was awarded United Nations Person of the Year.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tegla_Loroupe#cite_note-16)

# Khalid Khannouchi
![Image 31: Bronze medal – third place](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/60/Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg/20px-Bronze_medal_icon_%28B_initial%29.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)[2000 London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_London_Marathon "2000 London Marathon")[Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon")
**Khalid Khannouchi** ([Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): خالد خنّوشي) (born September 12, 1971) is a [Moroccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco "Morocco")-born American retired [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running"). He is the former [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_world_records_in_athletics "List of world records in athletics") holder for the marathon and held the former road world best for the [20 km](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_running "Road running") distance. He is one of only five men to break the marathon world record more than once, and one of only five to break their own marathon world record (the others are [Jim Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Peters_(athlete) "James Peters (athlete)"), [Derek Clayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Clayton "Derek Clayton"), [Eliud Kipchoge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliud_Kipchoge "Eliud Kipchoge"), and [Haile Gebrselassie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Gebrselassie "Haile Gebrselassie")).

# Khalid Khannouchi
Khalid fell out with the Moroccan athletics federation over training expenses and moved to [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") in 1992 with three of his friends. He married American Sandra Inoa in 1996, who coached him and acted as his [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent"). They set up home in [Ossining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossining_(town),_New_York "Ossining (town), New York"), [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)"). He became a [naturalized citizen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalized_citizen "Naturalized citizen") of the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") on May 2, 2000. He first gained broad renown by winning the [1997 Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_Chicago_Marathon "1997 Chicago Marathon") by over a minute with a time of 2:07.10, breaking the 12-year old course record held by [Steve Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jones_(runner) "Steve Jones (runner)").
Khannouchi officially retired on March 27, 2012 due to recurring foot injuries since 2003. Khannouchi stated "It was really my feet that betrayed me. Every time I go and try to push hard, I get the pain and soreness again. I can't train hard and if you can't train at a certain level where you can be competitive it's not worth it to keep wasting time."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalid_Khannouchi#cite_note-1)

## Achievements
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Khalid_Khannouchi&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Achievements")]
*   1993   
    *   [World Student Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Summer_Universiade "1993 Summer Universiade"), winner of the men's [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") in [Buffalo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York").

*   1997   
    *   Cobán Half Marathon (Guatemala), winner (1:04:30).  
    *   [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon"), winner (2:07:10), at that time the fastest debut marathon in history and the fourth fastest marathon of all time.

*   1998   
    *   Chicago Marathon, second place (2:07:19)  
    *   Peachtree Road Race 10k, winner (27:47)  
    *   Falmouth Road Race 7.1 miles, winner (31:48)  
    *   New Haven 20K, winner in a world road record (57:37)

*   1999   
    *   Chicago Marathon, winner in [world record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_world_best_progression "Marathon world best progression") time (2:05:42)  
    *   Peachtree Road Race 10k, winner (27:45)

*   2000   
    *   [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), third place (2:08:36)  
    *   [Chicago Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Marathon "Chicago Marathon"), winner in a new American record (2:07:01)

# Khalid Khannouchi
## Achievements
*   2002   
    *   London Marathon, winner in world record time (2:05:38)  
    *   Chicago Marathon, winner (2:05:56), becoming the first man in history to break 2:06 twice in one year  
    *   Ranked as the number #1 marathoner in the world by [Track & Field News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Track_&_Field_News "Track & Field News") and their American Athlete of the Year.

*   2004   
    *   Chicago Marathon, fifth place (2:08:44)

*   2006   
    *   [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), 4th place (2:07:04), coming back from a long period of injury.

*   2007   
    *   [London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_Marathon "London Marathon"), did not finish.  
    *   United States Olympic Marathon Trials in New York City, 4th place (2:12:34)[](https://web.archive.org/web/20100406052024/http://www.runnersworld.com/article/0,7120,s6-239-399--12281-0,00.html)
Khannouchi was the first marathoner to break 2:06:00. However, he lost the world record to [Paul Tergat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Tergat "Paul Tergat") on September 28, 2003.

# Vivian Cheruiyot
**Vivian Jepkemoi Cheruiyot** (born 11 September 1983)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-WAprofile-2) is a Kenyan [long-distance runner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_running "Long-distance running"). She represented Kenya at the [Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the Summer Olympics") in 2000, 2008, 2012, and 2016, winning the silver medal in the [5,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres") and bronze in the [10,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/10,000_metres "10,000 metres") at the [2012 London Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2012 Summer Olympics") as well as gold in the 5,000 m and silver in the 10,000 m at the [2016 Rio Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics"), setting a new [Olympic record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_records_in_athletics "List of Olympic records in athletics") in the former.

# Vivian Cheruiyot
Cheruiyot won the silver medal in the 5,000 m at the [2007 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2007 World Championships in Athletics") and became the world champion in the event at the [2009 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics"), repeating this achievement in [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2011 World Championships in Athletics"), when she also won the 10,000 m. She added gold for the latter event at the [2015 World Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2015 World Championships in Athletics"). After taking a silver in the [3,000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres") at the [2010 World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2010 IAAF World Indoor Championships"), Cheruiyot won a number of outdoor 5,000 m titles that year, becoming [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games "Athletics at the 2010 Commonwealth Games"), [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2010 African Championships in Athletics") and [Continental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_IAAF_Continental_Cup "2010 IAAF Continental Cup") champion, as well as winning the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_IAAF_Diamond_League "2010 IAAF Diamond League") title.

# Vivian Cheruiyot
She is a three-time Diamond League champion, having also won the [2011](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_IAAF_Diamond_League "2011 IAAF Diamond League") and [2012](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_IAAF_Diamond_League "2012 IAAF Diamond League") editions. She is the [Kenyan record](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Kenyan_records_in_athletics "List of Kenyan records in athletics") holder for the [2,000 m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_metres "2000 metres") and 10,000 m. In 2012, Cheruiyot was voted [Laureus World Sportswoman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureus_World_Sports_Award_for_Sportswoman_of_the_Year "Laureus World Sports Award for Sportswoman of the Year"). She is nicknamed "**pocket rocket**".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-3)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Vivian_Cheruiyot&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Career")]
Vivian Cheruiyot is trained by Ricky Simms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-4) She was born near [Keiyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keiyo "Keiyo") in the [Rift Valley Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rift_Valley_Province "Rift Valley Province"), coming from the same village as another female runner [Alice Timbilili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Timbilili "Alice Timbilili").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-5)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
Her breakthrough year came in 1999: at the age of fifteen she took the junior silver medal at the [1999 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "1999 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") behind [Werknesh Kidane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Werknesh_Kidane "Werknesh Kidane"). At the [1999 World Youth Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1999_World_Youth_Championships_in_Athletics "1999 World Youth Championships in Athletics") she won the bronze medal in the [3000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3000_metres "3000 metres"). Cheruiyot earned a senior call-up for the [1999 All-Africa Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_1999_All-Africa_Games "Athletics at the 1999 All-Africa Games"), where she managed a bronze medal in the [5000 metres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5000_metres "5000 metres"). She became the junior champion at the [2000 IAAF World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2000 IAAF World Cross Country Championships"). Cheruiyot gained selection for the [2000 Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Athletics at the 2000 Summer Olympics") and reached the 5000 m final after setting personal bests in the qualifying rounds. She was much slower in the final and was the last runner to finish.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-6)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
Cheruiyot won the silver medal at the 5000 m final of the [2007 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2007 World Championships in Athletics") in [Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osaka "Osaka"), Japan with a time of 14:58.50, behind [Meseret Defar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meseret_Defar "Meseret Defar") in 14:57.91.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-7)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
In early 2009 she broke the Kenyan indoor 3000 m record with a time of 8:30.53 in [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), and won the [World's Best 10K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Best_10K "World's Best 10K") race in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-8) In May, she won the [Great Manchester Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Manchester_Run "Great Manchester Run") 10K race. Cheruiyot won the women's 5000 m at the [2009 World Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_World_Championships_in_Athletics "2009 World Championships in Athletics") in [Berlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berlin "Berlin") with a time of 14 minutes 58.33 seconds, while countrywoman [Sylvia Kibet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sylvia_Kibet "Sylvia Kibet") took the silver. She closed the track season with a 3000 m silver and a 5000 m bronze at the [2009 IAAF World Athletics Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_IAAF_World_Athletics_Final "2009 IAAF World Athletics Final"). She won the 2009 New Year's Eve [San Silvestre Vallecana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Silvestre_Vallecana "San Silvestre Vallecana") race.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-9)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
Cheruiyot retained her World's Best 10K title in 2010.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-10) An appearance at the [2010 IAAF World Indoor Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_IAAF_World_Indoor_Championships "2010 IAAF World Indoor Championships") resulted in a silver medal in the 3000 m behind Meseret Defar. Cheruiyot then headed the Kenyan 5000 m challenge at the [African Championships in Athletics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_African_Championships_in_Athletics "2010 African Championships in Athletics") in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi") and beat Defar on this occasion to take the African title.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-11) After this, her main focus of the year was the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_IAAF_Diamond_League "2010 IAAF Diamond League").

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
She took victories in the 5000 m at the [Meeting Areva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meeting_Areva "Meeting Areva") and [Memorial van Damme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_van_Damme "Memorial van Damme") and was elected the inaugural Diamond League Trophy winner for the event on overall points.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-12) She defeated [Sentayehu Ejigu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sentayehu_Ejigu "Sentayehu Ejigu") at the [Continental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_IAAF_Continental_Cup "2010 IAAF Continental Cup") to take the 5000 m gold medal for Africa.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-13) Another gold medal in the event came at the [Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletics_at_the_2010_Commonwealth_Games "Athletics at the 2010 Commonwealth Games") held that year in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi"), where she headed a Kenyan podium sweep with Sylvia Kibet and [Ines Chenonge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ines_Chenonge "Ines Chenonge").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-14) Cheruiyot returned to Kenya to train and took an 8 km win at the [Tuskys Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuskys_Cross_Country "Tuskys Cross Country") meeting.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-15) She ended the year on a high note with a win at the [BOclassic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BOclassic "BOclassic") 5K race on New Year's Eve.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-16)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
Cheruiyot began preparing for the [World Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_IAAF_World_Cross_Country_Championships "2011 IAAF World Cross Country Championships") in January 2011 and came third at the [Great Edinburgh Cross Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Edinburgh_Cross_Country "Great Edinburgh Cross Country") before overhauling [Linet Masai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linet_Masai "Linet Masai") to win the [Cross de Itálica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_de_It%C3%A1lica "Cross de Itálica") in Seville.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-18) A second-place finish at the [Kenyan Cross Country Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenyan_Cross_Country_Championships "Kenyan Cross Country Championships") guaranteed her a place in the Kenyan squad and, in contrast to her successes on the track, she was looking to win her first cross country medal on the world stage.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-19) Her rival Masai led the initial charge at the World Cross Country Championships, but Cheruiyot broke away on the final lap to secure the gold medal and lead Kenya to the women's team title.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-20)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
She started 2012 with a win at the [World's Best 10K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Best_10K "World's Best 10K") and improved her best on the roads to 30:47 minutes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-21) She opened the [Diamond League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Diamond_League "2012 Diamond League") circuit with narrow wins ahead of Meseret Defar, first in the 3000 m in Doha and then over 5000 m in Rome.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-22) Cheruiyot guaranteed her place at the Olympics by winning the 10,000 m trial in Nairobi in June.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-23) At the Olympics, she won the silver medal in the 5000 metres and a bronze at the 10,000 metres.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-sports-reference-1)
In 2018, she won the [2018 London Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_London_Marathon "2018 London Marathon") with a time of 2:18:31.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-WAprofile-2)

# Vivian Cheruiyot
## Career
She took second place in the [2018 New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_New_York_City_Marathon "2018 New York City Marathon"), finishing in 2:26:02 far behind winner [Mary Keitany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Keitany "Mary Keitany") in 2:22:48, and 20 seconds ahead of [Shalane Flanagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shalane_Flanagan "Shalane Flanagan") who ran 2:26:22.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Cheruiyot#cite_note-24)
